semantic_distinctions.name: finite termination
semantic_distinctions.meaning: Execution reaches a finite terminal outcome; normal return is one possible subcase depending on the source semantics.

semantic_distinctions.name: silent nontermination
semantic_distinctions.meaning: Execution continues indefinitely after a finite observable prefix without producing further observable events.

semantic_distinctions.name: reactive nontermination
semantic_distinctions.meaning: Execution continues indefinitely while producing an infinite observable trace.

semantic_distinctions.name: going wrong / undefined behavior boundary
semantic_distinctions.meaning: An erroneous or semantically undefined execution class; must not be conflated with valid nontermination.

semantic_distinctions.name: partial correctness
semantic_distinctions.meaning: A postcondition conditional on the relevant return outcome; does not by itself exclude nontermination.

semantic_distinctions.name: termination / total correctness
semantic_distinctions.meaning: Requires an additional finite-progress or normal-return obligation beyond partial correctness.

techniques.mechanism: coinductive-style infinite execution relations plus forward/backward simulation lemmas
techniques.preserved_observations: finite traces for silent divergence and infinite traces for reactive divergence
techniques.boundary: sequential trace semantics; no general scheduler-fairness or Rust-specific UB model

techniques.mechanism: Lean partial_fixpoint over Result with Result.div as bottom
techniques.proof_of_success: standard WP.spec excludes fail and div for the proved invocation
techniques.boundary: frontend does not map every infinite Rust source shape into Result.div; NoBreak loops are rejected at this pin

anti_inferences: can_diverge=true proves divergence on a particular input
target final-value agreement covers nonterminating source executions
a target bottom/divergence value implies complete source-language nontermination coverage
Rust diverging expression means semantic infinite execution
